description: Takes a plain-language data question (official statistics, central bank rates, FX, energy, weather, holidays, research metadata). By default (mode "auto") it does not guess a value: like find_data it returns outcome "candidates" with up to 10 labelled series (publisher title, place with code and level, unit, latest value, range, source, licence) and the call_api arguments of each, or outcome "none" with a reason. Choose the candidate whose measure, place and time match the question and pass its call_api arguments to call_api: that second call returns the value. If none matches, tell the user this service does not have it. mode "strict" instead routes the question to one endpoint, runs it and returns the value with answered_with (compare it with your question before you use it), or "unfulfilled"; a value history then holds only the newest values, full true returns all of it. Examples: "germany inflation", "unemployment rate california 2024". When to use: for any data question when you do not know the endpoint id. For a task with several figures or countries pass questions, not one call each. Use call_api instead when you already have an id, get_series for a long numeric history. Read-only, no API key or signup. Free quota: 1000 calls/day per IP, shared across tools.

full.description: mode strict: true returns the whole value history (default: only the newest values and those of the years asked for, see truncated).

mode.description: auto (default): candidates to choose from, no value on a guess. strict: one routed value or "unfulfilled", for callers that cannot make a second call.

questions.description: Several questions answered in one call, in place of query. Split a task into one question per figure and place, e.g. ["inflation chile", "inflation peru"]. Each counts as one call of the quota.

name: ask_anything
title: Answer a data question
